title: Drop a penny off the Empire State Building with no air and it hits at 311 km/h

beats.say: What if you dropped a penny off the Empire State Building with no air? It hits the street at 311 kilometres an hour.
beats.speak: What if you dropped a penny off the Empire State Building with no air? It hits the street at three hundred and eleven kilometres an hour.

head: WHY
beats.say: From the 381 metre roof, it falls for about 8.8 seconds and lands at 86.5 metres per second.
beats.speak: From the three hundred and eighty one metre roof, it falls for about eight point eight seconds and lands at eighty six point five metres per second.

head: TWICE AS HIGH.
TWICE AS FAST?
beats.say: Make the drop twice as high, 762 metres. It is only 41% faster: 440 kilometres an hour.
beats.speak: Make the drop twice as high, seven hundred and sixty two metres. It is only forty one percent faster: four hundred and forty kilometres an hour.

head: NOW DROP IT
FROM DEEP SPACE.
beats.say: Now let it fall in from deep space. It hits at Earth's escape velocity: 40,270 kilometres an hour.
beats.speak: Now let it fall in from deep space. It comes in at the escape velocity of Earth: forty thousand two hundred and seventy kilometres an hour.

head: A PENNY THAT
HITS LIKE A CAR.
beats.say: That 2.5 gram penny now hits with 156,408 joules. Same as a 1500 kilogram car at 52 kilometres an hour.
beats.speak: That two point five gram penny now hits with one hundred and fifty six thousand four hundred and eight joules. Same as a fifteen hundred kilogram car at fifty two kilometres an hour.

head: NOW MAKE IT
A METEOR.
beats.say: Now throw it in as fast as the fastest meteors, 72 kilometres per second.
beats.speak: Now throw it in as fast as the fastest meteor, seventy two kilometres per second.

head: ONE PENNY.
11 CARS.
beats.say: It lands with 6.48 million joules. Like 11 cars, 1500 kilograms each, hitting at 100 kilometres an hour.
beats.speak: It lands with six point four eight million joules. Like eleven cars, fifteen hundred kilograms each, hitting at one hundred kilometres an hour.

head: REALITY
CHECK.
beats.say: With real air, a penny tops out at about 40 kilometres an hour after just 15 metres. When test pennies hit physicist Louis Bloomfield, it did not hurt.
beats.speak: With real air, a penny tops out at about forty kilometres an hour after just fifteen metres. When test pennies hit physicist Louis Bloomfield, it did not hurt.

beats.say: Penny or ballpoint pen: which is more dangerous to drop? Comment.

caption: Drop a 2.5 g penny off the Empire State Building's 381 m roof with no air: it falls for about 8.8 seconds and hits at 86.5 m/s, 311 km/h. Twice the height (762 m) is only 41% faster, 440 km/h, because speed grows with the square root of height. Let it fall in from deep space and it arrives at Earth's escape velocity, 11.186 km/s (40,270 km/h, 129 times faster), carrying 156,408 joules: the energy of a 1500 kg car at 52 km/h. At the fastest meteor speed, 72 km/s, it carries 6.48 million joules, as much as 11 of those cars at 100 km/h. Reality check: with air, a penny tops out at about 40 km/h after about 15 m of falling, and when test pennies hit physicist Louis Bloomfield, it did not hurt.
notes: US Mint coin specifications: Cent weight 2.500 g. Britannica summary: 'At a height of 1,250 ft (381 m)'; ESB facts and figures: 1,250 feet to its highest occupied floor (380 m on that page; 381 m used per Britannica). NASA NSSDC Earth fact sheet: GM 0.39860 x 10^6 km3/s2 (398,600 km3/s2), volumetric mean radius 6371.000 km, escape velocity 11.186 km/s. AMS Meteor FAQ: 'Meteors enter the atmosphere at speeds ranging from 11 km/sec (25,000 mph), to 72 km/sec (160,000 mph!)'. Scientific American (Life's Little Mysteries, 2012): pennies reach terminal velocity 'after only about 50 feet (15 meters)' and 'flutter to the ground at a measly 25 mph (40 kph), Bloomfield said'; 'When experimental pennies struck him, it didn't hurt'. UVA Today: a penny 'would most likely not kill someone if tossed from the Empire State Building'; Bloomfield: 'falling ballpoint pens are the real danger' (source for the comment question, which states no answer). Impact speeds use energy conservation with Newtonian gravity, v = sqrt(2 GM (1/R - 1/(R+h))), no air, Earth's rotation ignored. Fall time t = sqrt(2h/g0) with g0 = GM/R^2 (constant g over 381 m), about 8.8 s. Falling from rest at a great distance arrives at the escape velocity by definition (sqrt(2GM/R) = 11.186 km/s from these inputs). 1500 kg car is a chosen example mass (constant), 100 km/h a chosen comparison speed (constant). The 72 km/s case is a thought experiment that ignores the atmosphere (a real penny would burn and slow in air). Kinetic energy 0.5 m v^2. Series: 12 earlier posted what-if lines in log.jsonl, so this is What if #13 (series_n = 12 + 1).
